Review Whisper by OpenAI?

Reviewers see Whisper as an unusually strong speech-to-text engine, praised for accurate transcription across accents, noisy audio, multiple languages, and even mid-sentence code-switching. Users also value that it can run locally or offline for privacy-sensitive work. Founders of products like Scholé and Lispr echo that, citing low latency, multilingual dictation, and real product use. The main caveats are practical: setup can be technical, official client tooling is thin, and occasional hallucinated text means some teams still avoid blind trust.

+39

Pros

Cons

Reviews [...] Multilingual accuracy is what actually sold us most speech-to-text I'd tried before handled English fine and fell apart the moment a conversation switched languages mid-sentence, which happens constantly for us. Whisper handles code-switching a lot better than anything else we tested. Being open source and able to run offline mattered just as much we're processing voice notes that sometimes include unreleased product details, and sending that audio to a third-party API felt like the wrong trade before we'd even shipped anything.

#### What needs improvement [...] Whisper is honestly one of the most impressive AI tools OpenAI has released. The transcription accuracy is insanely good, especially for different accents and noisy audio, and being able to run it locally is a huge plus for privacy. It’s not perfect though — it can occasionally hallucinate text, so I wouldn’t trust it blindly for medical/legal stuff. Setup can also feel a bit technical if you’re not familiar with AI tools or command-line workflows. But overall, Reddit/dev communities still treat Whisper as one of the best and most reliable speech-to-text engines available today.
